text.title: Feature Prioritisation — RICE Core Rules
text.summary: Testable rules grounding Feature Prioritisation — RICE. Each pairs a binary check with a sourced rationale; HARD rules — user-supplied input cannot override. RICE formula definition, scale for each of the four factors, scoring process, and constraints for valid scores.

section.title: Background
section.p: Reach. Number of users/customers affected per quarter. Source from analytics (funnel data, MAU counts, segment sizes). Never use "everyone" — estimate the segment.

list.item: 100% — data-backed and tested (prototype results, A/B test, analytics correlation)
80% — some data, reasonable assumptions, similar feature precedent
50% — opinions, limited data, no prior evidence
0.5 — a few days (patch, copy change, minor config)

rule.statement: Score = Reach × Impact × Confidence ÷ Effort. All 4 dimensions mandatory.
rule.rationale: Score = Reach × Impact × Confidence ÷ Effort. All 4 dimensions mandatory.

rule.statement: Items with confidence <50% require a spike before scoring.
rule.rationale: Items with confidence <50% require a spike before scoring.

rule.statement: Items with effort >2 person-weeks require split or spike before scoring.
rule.rationale: Items with effort >2 person-weeks require split or spike before scoring.

rule.statement: Reach unit (e.g. users/quarter) and effort unit (person-weeks) consistent across the batch.
rule.rationale: Reach unit (e.g. users/quarter) and effort unit (person-weeks) consistent across the batch.

rule.statement: Top item is captured as a decision record with the scoring table attached.
rule.rationale: Top item is captured as a decision record with the scoring table attached.

rule.statement: RICE Score = (Reach x Impact x Confidence) / Effort. Express Reach in the same unit (users/quarter) for the entire batch. Never mix monthly and quarterly denominators.
rule.rationale: Mixing time periods inflates some rows 3-4x, making the ranking meaningless. Consistency in Reach units is more important than precision.

rule.statement: Use only the fixed Impact scale: 3 (massive), 2 (high), 1 (medium), 0.5 (low), 0.25 (minimal). Never invent intermediate values.
rule.rationale: Intermediate values (1.7, 2.3) create false precision and destroy cross-feature comparability. The fixed scale forces explicit categorization.

rule.statement: Cap Confidence at 50% for any item without a cited evidence URL or table reference. Reserve 100% for data-backed, tested items only.
rule.rationale: Agents and humans default to 80-100% when uncomfortable. Evidence requirement prevents confidence inflation that produces false precision scores.

rule.statement: Express Effort in total person-months including design, dev, QA, and docs. Require a breakdown before accepting any estimate.
rule.rationale: LLMs under-estimate effort 2-3x when not broken down. Decomposing into sub-disciplines exposes hidden work and produces calibrated estimates.

rule.statement: Re-score quarterly. Archive prior scoring files with date stamp to detect drift.
rule.rationale: Stale scores produce wrong roadmaps. Feature importance shifts as the product grows and user segments change.

rule.statement: If preconditions in AGENTS.md "Applies If" do not all hold, OR any "Skip If" disqualifier is true, do not run this methodology — route to the named alternative.
rule.rationale: Methodologies are pre-condition gated; running them out-of-scope produces noise and burns the agent context budget.

rule.statement: If preconditions hold, execute the procedure in `content/04-procedure.xml` (or the rule set above when complexity is light), emit the artefact specified by `content/02-output-contract.xml`, and validate with `scripts/validate-feature-prioritization-rice.py` before returning.
rule.rationale: Tying the entry rule to the validator script closes the loop between policy and machine check.
